end.summary:
Named polygons by number of sides: triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon, and octagon.
Recognised triangles and polygons despite changes in position and size.
Described triangles using equal sides and right angles.
Explained that a D shape is not a polygon because it has a curved side.
Applied polygon side counts to composite-shape questions; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Veer practised naming polygons, spotting them in different positions and sizes, and describing triangles by equal sides and angles. They used the method of counting straight sides and corners, and correctly explained why a D shape is not a polygon. They also worked through right-angled isosceles triangles and splitting a square into two triangles; no recorded misconception remained. At home, ask Veer to find household shapes and name each polygon by counting its straight sides.
